name: Indian Peafowl
desc: The Indian Peafowl or Indian Blue Peafowl is a large bird and probably the only largest one that can fly. The males are called peacocks, while the females are called peahens. Together, they are peafowl. The male is one of the most recognisable birds in the world. It has around 20 brown tail feathers which are much shorter and support his fan display. It is also the national bird of India.

name: Rose-ringed Parakeet
desc: The Rose-ringed Parakeet is native to Asia and Africa. They are mainly green in colour with a red bill and a long, tapered tail. Because of their green colour, they are very difficult to see during roosting or perching in trees.

name: Plum-headed Parakeet
desc: The Plum-headed Parakeet is mainly green, with the male having a red head and the female a bluish grey head. This bird lives in forests and open woodlands, and is sometimes seen in city gardens.

name: Red-vented Bulbul
desc: The Red-vented Bulbul is a small sized bird in the bulbul family. Their diet consists mainly of fruits, berries, and insects. It is easily identified by the bright red colour on the vent and this also reflects in its name. Males and females look similar though the males are slightly larger.

name: Coppersmith Barbet
desc: Coppersmith Barbet are close relatives of woodpeckers and they too make a hole in the tree for nesting. It is a resident bird found in throughout South Asia, it is a round and plump bird. The head is large and has a short neck and tail.

name: Common Iora
desc: The Common Iora is a small, brightly coloured passerine bird found throughout Indian subcontinent. These birds are quite vocal and can produce a wide variety of calls. The most commonly heard is the whistle “twiii tuiii twiiii.” Apart from this, it utters variable “chirrs” and chattering.

name: Purple Sunbird
desc: The Purple Sunbird is a very small sunbird. Like all sunbirds they feed mainly on nectar but they take up insects while feeding their young ones. They have a down-curved bill with brush-tipped tubular tongues that aid in nectar feeding.

name: Greater Coucal
desc: The Greater Coucal is a large bird of the cuckoo family and is also known as Crow Pheasant. Its sighting is also considered auspicious. In India the bird is known as Bhardwaj. Both the sexes are identical but females are bit larger.

name: Asian Koel
desc: Asian Koel is a member of the cuckoo family of birds. Koels are highly frugivorous as their diet consists entirely of fruit. During hard winters they migrate to warmer areas. Asian koel like many of its related cuckoo kin is a brood parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of crows and other hosts, who raise its young.

name: Indian Grey Hornbill
desc: The Indian Grey Hornbill is a medium-sized bird found only in the Indian subcontinent. It is one of the nine species of hornbills seen in India. These birds nest in old hollows in large trees. The female bird enters the hollow and seals herself inside. During her long internment inside the nest, the male bird feeds her through a narrow slit with berries.

name: Indian Roller
desc: The Indian Roller is widely found across its range. The local name of the Indian Roller is Neelkanth (meaning “blue throat”), a name associated with the deity Shiva (who drank poison resulting in the blue throat). It is considered sacred among the Hindus. The bird is well known for its aerobatic displays during the breeding season and hence this “roller” word in its name.

name: Brahminy Starling
desc: The Brahminy Starling is also known as Brahminy Myna is a small robin sized bird. It is very sociable and are often seen in pairs, or large flocks, throughout India. It has a distinctive crest formed by extended crown feathers.

name: Common Tailorbird
desc: Common Tailorbird is the most common singing bird found across Asia, except desert areas. The typical nest is built by sewing the leaves together and hence Common Tailorbird gets its name.

name: Yellow-throated Sparrow
desc: The Yellow-throated Sparrow is a species of sparrow-like bird. It is also known as Chestnut-shouldered Petronia. The male has an indistinct eyebrow, an inconspicuous pale yellow spot on the throat, and light chestnut on the shoulders.

name: Indian Silverbill
desc: The Indian Silverbill is a small passerine bird found all over the Indian Subcontinent. This bird gets its name due to its silver coloured beak. It is described as the dullest bird, as both sexes, as well as juveniles, are similar in colour. They are entirely non-migratory.

name: Indian Robin
desc: The Indian Robin is a small sized bird commonly found throughout the Indian subcontinent. They are especially found in open, bushy areas. They are commonly observed running on the ground or perched on low shrubs and rocks.

name: Ashy Prinia
desc: The Ashy Prinia is a small warbler that is commonly found in city gardens and farmlands. It is of a restrained nature and hops about quietly among the bushes in search of insects, only uttering a sharp “tee-tee-tee” from time to time.

name: Oriental Magpie-robin
desc: The Oriental Magpie-Robin is a small black and white passerine bird found all over India. It is a very melodious singer and sings with different notes. They are common birds in urban gardens as well as forests.

name: White-browed Fantail
desc: The White-browed Fantail is a widely distributed species in tropical regions of the Indian subcontinent. This bird is named for its fan-like tail. An adult is about 18 cm long. It has dark brown upper parts with white spots on the wings, whitish underparts, and a fan shaped tail is edged in white.

name: Green Bee-eater
desc: The Green Bee-eater is a small sized bird with bright green plumage and a long tail. It is well known for its aerial acrobatics which it performs to catch insects in flight. After spotting an insect, it flies after its prey snapping it in mid-air, and then circles back to its perch. It then hits the prey on the branch to make it tender or remove the sting before eating it.

name: White-browed Wagtail
desc: The White-browed Wagtail can be easily identified by its size, the white brow on the head, and its characteristic long, constantly wagging tail. This distinctive behaviour is likely the reason behind its name in Gujarati.

name: Red-wattled Lapwing
desc: The Red-wattled Lapwing is long-legged bird from the plover family, widely found all over India. They are locally known as the “did-he-do-it” bird due to its unmistakable call.

name: White-throated Kingfisher
desc: White-throated Kingfisher is often found well away from water, commonly on top of buildings and wires. It dives to catch aquatic prey feet-first in shallow water and head-first in deeper areas. They are very vocal birds and the call of this kingfisher is a chuckling “chake-ake-ake-ake-ake”.

name: Indian Cormorant
desc: Indian Cormorants (Indian Shags) exhibit unique behaviours, including fishing communally, making short dives for prey, and drying their wings with outstretched wings after swimming. They are known for their gregarious fishing habits, often seen in groups driving fish into corners.

name: Savanna Nightjar
desc: The Savanna Nightjar is a nocturnal, insectivorous bird. These birds begin vocalisation during early dusk and can be heard throughout the night until dawn, becoming especially vocal during the breeding season. The "chwip" call is used for both marking territory and attracting females during the breeding season.

name: River Tern
desc: A graceful river bird with a slender body, grey upperparts, white underparts and a bright orange bill with a black tip. It catches fish by plunging into rivers and lakes.

name: Grey Heron
desc: A large, long-legged wading bird with grey wings, a white head and a long yellow bill. It stands patiently in shallow water and feeds mainly on fish.

name: Indian Pond Heron
desc: A stocky, well-camouflaged heron, usually brown and streaked when resting. In flight it reveals striking white wings; it hunts fish, frogs and insects.

name: Indian Vulture
desc: A large scavenging bird with broad wings, a pale body and a dark flight-feather edge. It feeds mainly on carrion and is critically endangered.

name: Egyptian Vulture
desc: A smaller, pale vulture with a yellow face and wedge-shaped tail. It feeds on carrion and scraps, and is known to use stones to crack large eggs.

name: Black-winged Kite
desc: A small, elegant raptor with a white body, grey back, black shoulder patches and red eyes. It often hovers over open grassland while hunting rodents.

name: Northern Shoveler
desc: A dabbling duck recognised by its broad, spoon-shaped bill. It sweeps the bill through shallow water to filter tiny plants and animals.

name: Little Grebe
desc: A tiny waterbird with a compact body and short neck. It dives underwater to catch small fish and aquatic invertebrates.

name: Eurasian Hoopoe
desc: An unmistakable bird with a tall fan-shaped crest, warm cinnamon plumage and black-and-white wings. It probes the ground with its long curved bill for insects.

name: Crested Serpent Eagle
desc: A forest-dwelling eagle with a prominent crest, broad rounded wings and yellow facial skin. It hunts snakes and other reptiles, as well as small animals.

name: Black-winged Stilt
desc: A striking wader with extremely long pink legs, a slender black bill and contrasting black-and-white plumage. It feeds in shallow wetlands.

name: Indian Rock Eagle-Owl
desc: A large, powerful owl with prominent ear tufts, orange eyes and mottled brown plumage. It roosts on rocky slopes and is most active at dusk and night.

name: Black-tailed Godwit
desc: A tall wading bird with long legs and a long, straight bill. Its breeding plumage is chestnut-toned; it probes wet mud for worms and other small prey.

name: Ruddy Shelduck
desc: A large orange-brown waterfowl with a pale head and black flight feathers. Often seen in pairs, it uses lakes and wetlands for feeding and resting.

name: Northern Pintail
desc: A graceful dabbling duck. The male has a chocolate-brown head, white neck stripe and long pointed tail feathers; it feeds in shallow water.
